translationRepairs: Emperor Jing, taboo name Shi, courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi).
Emperor Jing, taboo name Shi, courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan.
The focus unit names only 景皇帝, 師, 子元, and 宣帝. Its parenthetical “Sima Yi” is not in the source; removing that supplied name restores a literal translation.

At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor named Sima Shi General Who Stabilizes the Army and regent in the combined office of Great General.

At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor appointed Sima Shi General Who Pacifies the Army to assist in government.
撫軍大將軍 is one office and 輔政 means assisting in government. “General Who Pacifies the Army” avoids the proposed awkward office expansion while removing the invented combined post and regency.
Sima Shi wept and said, "My forebears enjoyed extraordinary favor from the house of Wei; the late emperor, on his deathbed, bound us with his final charge.
Sima Shi wept and said, "My late father received extraordinary favor through successive reigns; when the late emperor was dying, he entrusted him with a testamentary edict.

Here 先臣 is Sima Shi’s deferential reference to his deceased father, not biological forebears or an unspecified plural of officials. The revised wording keeps the personal relation and the testamentary entrustment.
Pure Music assistant Pang Xi’s pleas went unheeded.
When the Assistant Director of Pure Music Pang Xi remonstrated with the emperor, the emperor did not listen.
清商丞龐熙諫帝，帝弗聽 explicitly records Pang Xi’s remonstrance and the emperor’s refusal to listen. The proposed wording restores both omitted actions.
Let him ascend to the position of Chancellor of State, increase fief by nine thousand, together with the previous forty thousand households;
Let him ascend to the position of Chancellor of State and increase the fief by nine thousand households, making forty thousand households together with what he already held;
並前四萬戶 sets the combined fief at forty thousand households, including prior holdings. The prior literal wrongly reads it as nine thousand added to a pre-existing forty thousand.

Down to King Cheng of Zhou, the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao served as assistants; therefore they were able to depart from the classics and distinguish aims, secure the Way and rejoice in their tasks.
By the time of King Cheng of Zhou, Duke Dan and Grand Duke Wang served as his aides; therefore he could complete the Classics and set his aims, rest in the Way, and take joy in his work.

旦望 are Duke Dan and Grand Duke Wang, not the Duke of Shao; the king, not the two aides, is the subject of the resulting abilities. This wording also avoids overlapping the prior English title surfaces.
The Son of Heaven, receiving the seal, was lazy; lifting his toes high; the Emperor heard and worried about it.
The Son of Heaven, on receiving the seal, grew slack and walked with a high step; the Emperor heard of it and worried.
受璽惰，舉趾高 is a coordinated description of slack conduct and an arrogant gait. The proposal turns the broken literal clauses into that coherent judgment.
Under King Cheng the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao stood at his side, so the heir could move beyond rote text, fix his purpose, find peace in the Way, and take joy in ruling.
By the time of King Cheng of Zhou, Duke Dan and Grand Duke Wang served as his aides, so he could complete the Classics and set his aims, rest in the Way, and take joy in his work.

The idiomatic field also misidentifies 旦望 as the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao. The revision restores Duke Dan and Grand Duke Wang, keeps King Cheng as the subject, and avoids overlapping prior English title surfaces.
The commandant at Anfeng Ford ran him down, struck off his head, and sent it to Luoyang by post-horse.
The commandant at Anfeng Ford ran him down, struck off his head, and sent it to the capital by post-horse.
京都 says “the capital”; it does not identify Luoyang in this unit. The proposal removes the unsupported place-name while retaining the pursuit, beheading, and relay.
To give him the same posthumous wording as the two Wei founders fills me with dread.
To give him the same posthumous name as the two ancestors fills me with dread.
二祖 means “the two ancestors.” The source does not specify Wei founders, so the proposal removes an interpretive historical gloss from the idiomatic field.
Emperor Wen, personal name Zhao and courtesy name Zishang, was Sima Shi’s full younger brother.
Emperor Wen, personal name Zhao and courtesy name Zishang, was Sima Shi’s younger brother by the same mother.
母弟 specifies a younger brother sharing the mother; “full younger brother” improperly asserts shared father as well. The revision states the supplied kinship plainly.
When the great army punished Wang Ling, the Emperor supervised Huainan north military affairs and led troops to assemble at Xiang.
When the great army punished Wang Ling, the Emperor supervised military affairs north of the Huai and led troops to assemble at Xiang.
淮北 is the territory north of the Huai River, not “Huainan north.” The proposed literal corrects the geographical relation without changing the reported command.
The two armies suffered rout; by sitting he lost the marquisate.
The two armies suffered rout; he was held responsible and lost the marquisate.
坐 is legal responsibility in this context: the military defeat caused loss of the marquisate. The proposal removes the nonsensical literal “by sitting.”
Quan Yi’s mother was a daughter of Sun Quan; out of favor in Wu, she was escorted to the Wei lines by two nephews of Quan Duan.
Quan Yi’s mother was a daughter of Sun Quan. Having given offense in Wu, she fled over with Hui and Yi, sons of Quan Duan’s elder brother.
The unit names Hui and Yi and identifies them as sons of Quan Duan’s elder brother. The revision preserves those names and kinship without the ambiguous “her mother” in the proposal.
Quan Jing was still in Shouchun with Zhuge Dan; Zhong Hui forged letters in the names of the defectors to bait him.
Yi’s elder brother Jing was then in Shouchun; using Zhong Hui’s plan, they forged letters in Hui’s and Yi’s names to deceive Jing.
儀兄靜 places Yi’s elder brother Jing at Shouchun; 用鐘會計 attributes the stratagem to Zhong Hui, and 作禕、儀書 names the forged identities. The proposal removes the invented Zhuge Dan.
In the sixth month of summer, the fourth year, Jingzhou was split into two commands: Wang Ji took Xinye and Zhou Ta took Xiangyang.
In the sixth month of summer, the fourth year, Jingzhou was split into two commands: Wang Ji took Xinye and Zhou Tai took Xiangyang.
州泰 is the personal name Zhou Tai. The current idiomatic field truncates it to “Zhou Ta”; the proposed correction preserves the name consistently.

The Son of Heaven, because the Emperor for three generations was chief minister, government was not of himself issuing, inwardly could not be at peace, also feared deposition and humiliation, was about to ascend the gallery and summon the hundred officials and carry out dismissal.

The Son of Heaven, because the Emperor's house had been chief ministers for three generations, government was not issuing from himself, inwardly could not be at peace, also feared deposition and humiliation, was about to ascend the gallery and summon the hundred officials and carry out dismissal.
帝三世宰輔 refers to three generations of the Sima house holding chief-ministerial power, not one emperor serving as chief minister across three generations.
He sent his uncle Xun Yi in a litter to fetch Chen Tai into a side room and asked, "Xuanbo, what is the realm going to say of me now?"
He sent his maternal uncle Xun Yi in a litter to fetch Chen Tai into a side room and asked, "Xuanbo, what is the realm going to say of me now?"
舅 specifically denotes a maternal uncle. The proposed idiomatic translation makes that kinship explicit while preserving the rest of the scene.
Annoyed by Deng Ai’s foot-dragging, Sima Zhao made his chief clerk Shi Zuan Deng’s deputy to talk sense into him; Deng then accepted the order.
Annoyed by Deng Ai’s foot-dragging, Sima Zhao made his chief clerk Shi Zuan Deng Ai’s major to talk sense into him; Deng then accepted the order.
使主簿師纂為艾司馬 makes chief clerk Shi Zuan Deng Ai’s 司馬, a major; it does not fuse their names or appoint a generic deputy.

Yet you are quiet and respectful early and late, toiling and humble before dawn; although the Grandfather's assisting left and right civil and martial, Duke of Zhou's toil for the royal house—nothing is added beyond this.

Yet you are calm and reverent from dawn to dusk, laboring humbly before daylight; even Shangfu’s support in civil and military affairs and the Duke of Zhou’s toil for the royal house did not surpass it.
尚父 is the honorific Shangfu, not a grandfather. The revision also repairs the comparative grammar of 罔以加焉 while retaining the two historical comparisons.
When Huan and Wen saved the house of Zhou, they too received the nine gifts, that their great merit might shine as a pattern for posterity.

During the crises of Kings Hui and Xiang, Dukes Huan and Wen, for their work in protecting and supporting the throne, still received the rites of conferral; all this made the great virtue of earlier times shine as a model for later ages.
惠襄之難 and 錫命之禮 are both omitted or distorted by the current idiomatic field. The revision restores the crises and the rites of conferral without inventing the nine gifts.
We send a credential bearer, concurrent Minister of Education and metropolitan commandant, to hand you seal, ribbon, patent, gold beast tallies one through five, and bamboo tallies one through ten.

We order Gai, Bearer of Credentials, concurrent Minister of Education and Metropolitan Commandant, to confer at once the seal and ribbon, the patent, gold beast tallies one through five, and bamboo envoy tallies one through ten.
陔 is the named envoy, followed by 即授 (“confer at once”). The proposed idiomatic field restores Gai and accurately identifies the sequence of insignia.

Order Bearer of Credentials, concurrently Minister of Education, Metropolitan Commandant immediately to confer seal-ribbon and patent text, gold beast tallies first through fifth, bamboo envoy tallies first through tenth.

Order Bearer of Credentials, concurrently Minister of Education, Metropolitan Commandant Gai to confer at once the seal-ribbon and patent text, gold beast tallies first through fifth, bamboo envoy tallies first through tenth.
The same sequence identifies Gai as the envoy and 即授 as “confer at once.” The proposed literal fixes the prior parsing that dropped the person.
From your grandfather the chancellor onward, each generation has aided Wei with shining virtue until the court is clean of chaff and the people free of slander.
From the former Chancellor of State onward, each generation has aided Wei with shining virtue until the court is clean of chaff and the people free of slander.
先相國 means the former Chancellor of State. It supplies no kinship term, so “your grandfather” is unsupported and the proposed correction is warranted.
On bingwu the emperor named Sima Yan, the Central Stabilizing General and Marquis of Xinchang township, heir to the duchy of Jin.
On bingwu the emperor named Sima Yan, the Central Stabilizing General and Marquis of Xinchang township, heir apparent of Jin.
晉世子 is the heir apparent of Jin after the earlier elevation; it is not an heir to a duchy. The proposed wording gives the office correctly.
